title: Welsh Cawl
subtitle: Welsh lamb and leek broth, the national dish of Wales
excerpt: Cawl is the national dish of Wales: a thick, warming broth of lamb, leeks, and root vegetables that has been eaten in Welsh homes for centuries. It is traditionally made with neck of lamb or lamb on the bone, giving a richly flavoured broth. The dish is simple but deeply satisfying -- the leeks are what make it distinctively Welsh.
sourceNotes: Cawl (pronounced 'cowl') is the national dish of Wales. The word means broth or soup in Welsh. The dish has been made in Wales since at least the medieval period. Cawl is associated with Welsh national identity and is traditionally served on St David's Day (1 March). The version made in south Wales tends to be thicker; the northern Welsh version is lighter and brothier.

content.text: Neck of lamb on the bone gives the richest broth, as the collagen from the bones gives the cawl a slightly gelatinous quality. Shoulder chops are a good substitute. The leeks are added towards the end so they stay vibrant green and tender, not olive-grey and mushy. Traditionally cawl is served in two courses: the broth first, then the meat and vegetables.

content.text: Put {{lamb-shoulder}} lamb in a large pot with {{onion}} onion, {{bay-leaves}} bay leaves, {{thyme-fresh}} thyme, and 2.5 litres of cold water. Bring to a boil. Skim off any foam. Reduce to a steady simmer and cook for 1 hour.
Add {{carrots}} carrots, {{turnip}} turnip, {{swede}} swede, and {{potatoes-floury}} potatoes. Season with {{salt-table}} salt and {{black-pepper}} pepper. Continue simmering for 40 minutes.

Add {{leek}} leeks and cook for a further 15 minutes until tender but still green. Remove the {{lamb-shoulder}} lamb. Shred the meat from the bones and return to the pot. Scatter {{parsley-flat}} parsley over. Serve in large bowls with crusty bread.

items.symptom: The broth is thin and pale
items.cause: The lamb was not simmered long enough.
items.fix: Continue simmering. The collagen from the bones takes at least 1.5 hours to extract into the broth. The broth improves significantly overnight -- refrigerate and reheat the next day.

content.text: Cawl is the national dish of Wales. It is made in homes across the country, particularly on St David's Day (1 March). Recipes vary by region -- the south Welsh version uses more root vegetables and a thicker broth, while the northern Welsh cawl tends towards a clearer, lighter broth. Both are unmistakably Welsh in their reliance on local lamb and the leek, which is the national symbol of Wales.
